name: gizza-ai/smart-quotes-converter
summary: Convert quotes between straight ASCII and curly typographic form.

tool.description: Convert quotation marks between straight ASCII (" ') and curly typographic (“ ” ‘ ’) forms. direction='to_curly' (default) educates straight quotes into curly ones, choosing opening vs closing marks from the surrounding characters (start/space/bracket -> opening; after a letter/digit -> closing or apostrophe, e.g. It's, dogs', '89); direction='to_straight' reverses, turning curly quotes and prime marks back into plain ASCII (useful before pasting into code, CSV, or JSON). convert_double / convert_single (both default true) toggle each quote kind independently. feet_inches=true (to_curly only) turns digit-adjacent straight quotes into prime marks (6'4" -> 6′4″). Everything else — accents, CJK, emoji, dashes, ellipses — passes through untouched.

convert_double.description: Convert double quotes (" ⇄ “ ”). Set false to leave double quotes untouched. Default true.

convert_single.description: Convert single quotes and apostrophes (' ⇄ ‘ ’). Set false to leave them untouched. Default true.

direction.description: Conversion direction. 'to_curly' (default) turns straight ASCII quotes (" ') into curly typographic quotes (“ ” ‘ ’), choosing opening vs closing marks from the surrounding characters. 'to_straight' turns curly quotes (and prime marks) back into plain ASCII.

feet_inches.description: Feet/inches mode (to_curly only): a straight quote directly after a digit becomes a prime mark instead of a curly quote, so 6'4" becomes 6′4″. to_straight always folds prime marks back to ASCII regardless of this flag. Default false.

input.description: The text whose quotation marks you want to convert.
